about: This part finishes the fifth day and tells the sixth. Amoghasiddhi and his consort, who dawned at the end of the last part, come surrounded by two bodhisattvas and two female bodhisattvas, and from their heart the green light of the wisdom that accomplishes deeds pierces toward the dead man, together with the dull red light of the demigods, born of jealousy. He is to rest without fear in equanimity, since the light is the natural energy of his own awareness; failing that, he is to take refuge, give up clinging and say the prayer to Amoghasiddhi, and so become a buddha in the northern realm. Pointed out at so many stages, anyone with the least karmic connection will recognise one light or another; but those whose habitual tendencies are strong and who never grew familiar with pure vision are still driven on, and on the sixth day the five families dawn all at once, together with the six lights of the six kinds of beings. The reader tells the dead man why he is still here, and names the whole assembly coming to meet him: the four lights of the elements, the five buddhas and their consorts from their five realms, the eight gatekeepers, the six sages of the six realms, and Samantabhadra and Samantabhadrī, forty-two deities of the body of enjoyment. They come out of his own heart, whose four quarters and centre are their realms, and are present of themselves in his own awareness: he is to recognise them so.

sentences.w: སེམས་དཔའ་ ཕྱག་ན་རྡོ་རྗེ་ དང༔ སྒྲིབ་པ་རྣམ་བར་སེལ་བ་ གཉིས་ ལ༔ སེམས་མ་ གྷནྡྷེ་མ་ དང༔ ནཱིར་ཏི་མ་ གཉིས་ ཀྱིས་ བསྐོར་ ནས་ འཇའ་ དང་ འོད་ ཀྱི་ ཀློང་ ནས་ སངས་རྒྱས་ ཀྱི་ སྐུ་ དྲུག་ཏུ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: The hero Vajra-in-Hand and Obscurations-Completely-Clearing, two, with; the female-bodhisattvas Gandhā and Nṛtyā(?), two, by surrounded, then: rainbow and light's expanse from, buddha's bodies six-as dawning come.
sentences.i: Surrounded by the two bodhisattvas Vajrapāṇi and Sarvanivaraṇaviṣkambhin and the two female bodhisattvas Gandhā and Nṛtyā, they come to dawn as six buddha forms out of an expanse of rainbow and light.
sentences.n: The fifth day goes on from the end of the last part, where Amoghasiddhi and his consort dawned: the sentence follows the pattern of the days before. sems dpa', 'hero', stands for byang chub sems dpa', 'bodhisattva', as sems ma does for the female bodhisattvas. Phyag na rdo rje, 'Vajra in Hand' (Vajrapāṇi), and Sgrib pa rnam par sel ba, 'He Who Clears Away the Obscurations' (Sarvanivaraṇaviṣkambhin), are the bodhisattvas of the north. The print spells the second name rnam bar, its usual b for p; the letter of sgrib pa is also not sure on the image, where it may be ba, the same habit, and the sense is not touched. The female bodhisattvas' names are Sanskrit in Tibetan letters: གྷནྡྷེ (gandhe; the other recension གནྡྷེ) is the form of address of Gandhā, 'she of perfume' (gandha, 'scent'); ནཱིར་ཏི (nīr ti; the other recension ནིརྟི) is taken as Nṛtyā, 'she of dance' (nṛti, 'dancing', with its ṛ written as a vowel and r), the name that goes with Gandhā in the lists of the eight female bodhisattvas, but the letters do not spell it plainly. 'char du 'ong ngo, 'they come to dawn', where the days before had 'char nas 'ong ngo, 'they come dawning' (the other recension has nas here too); the sense is the same.

sentences.w: འདུ་བྱེད་ ཀྱི་ ཕུང་པོ་ གནས་སུ་ དག་པ་ འོད་ ལྗང་ཁུ་ བྱ་བ་ གྲུབ་པའི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ལྗང་ ལ་ འཆར་བ༔ གསལ་ ལ་ དྭངས་པ་ བཀྲག་ ལ་ ཉམས་ང་བ༔
sentences.l: Formation's aggregate in-its-place pure, light green, deeds accomplished's wisdom, green and dawning, bright and clear, lustrous and fearsome,
sentences.i: The aggregate of formations, pure in its own place, is the green light, the wisdom that accomplishes deeds: green and radiant, bright and clear, lustrous and fearsome,
sentences.n: As on the days before, with the fifth day's aggregate, colour and wisdom. 'du byed, 'formation, putting together' (Sanskrit saṃskāra), the fourth of the five aggregates: the impulses and habits by which the mind shapes what it does. bya ba grub pa'i ye shes, 'the wisdom by which what is to be done is accomplished' (bya ba, 'deed, what is to be done'; grub pa, 'accomplished'; Sanskrit kṛtyānuṣṭhānajñāna), is the wisdom of Amoghasiddhi. Here the print has no ༔ after dag pa. ljang la 'char ba, 'green and dawning', has 'char ba, 'dawning, shining forth', where the days before had 'tsher ba, 'shimmering'; bkrag la nyams nga ba, 'lustrous and fearsome', close to the words the print used of the pure vision of reality in 003. The other recension has ljang la 'tsher ba and bkrag mdangs can, 'lustrous', here.

sentences.w: ཐིག་ལེ་ དང་ ཐིག་ཕྲན་ གྱིས་ སྤྲས་པ་ ཅིག༔ དོན་ཡོད་གྲུབ་པ་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ གྱི་ ཐུགས་ཀ་ ནས་ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ སྙིང་ གི་ ཐད་ཀར་ མིག་ གིས་ མི་ བཟོད་པ་ ཙམ་དུ་ ཟུག་ ནས་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: drops and small-drops by adorned, one, Amoghasiddhi father-mother's heart from, you-yourself's heart's straight-at, eye by not bearable as-much-as, piercing comes.
sentences.i: adorned with drops and smaller drops. It comes piercing from the heart of Amoghasiddhi and his consort straight at your heart, so bright that your eyes can hardly bear it.
sentences.n: spras pa, 'adorned', a word of the same sense as the brgyan pa of the days before. cig, 'one', makes it 'a light', as gcig did there. The rest is the sentence of the fourth day word for word, with the fifth buddha's name; the other recension has mig gis blta mi bzod pa, 'unbearable for the eye to look at'.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་པར་ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ རིག་པའི་ རང་རྩལ་ ཡིན་པས་ ཆགས་སྡང་ ཉེ་རིང་ མེད་པའི་ བཏང་སྙོམས་ བྱར་མེད་ ཆེན་པོའི་ ངང་དུ་ ཞོག་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: That at not fearing-way, you-yourself's knowing's own-energy it-is-because: attachment-aversion near-far without's equanimity, nothing-to-do great's state-in rest!
sentences.i: Do not be afraid of it. It is the natural energy of your own awareness, so rest in equanimity, free of attachment and aversion, of near and far, in the great state where there is nothing to do.
sentences.n: This is new against the days before. rang rtsal, 'own energy, natural play' (rtsal, 'skill, power'): what awareness shows of itself, as rang mdangs, 'natural radiance', in 005; the other recension has rig pa'i ye shes kyi rang rtsal, 'the natural energy of the wisdom of awareness'. chags sdang, 'attachment and aversion', and nye ring, 'near and far', taking some things as one's own and others as strange, are the two pairs that equanimity is free of. btang snyoms, 'equanimity' (btang, 'let go'; snyoms, 'made even'). byar med chen po, 'great non-doing', the state of the fourth day's byar med kyi ngang, 'the state where there is nothing to do'. zhog cig, 'rest!', with zhog, the imperative of 'jog, 'to put, to leave'.

sentences.w: དེ་ དང་ མཉམ་དུ་ ལྷ་མ་ཡིན་ གྱི་ འོད་ དམར་པོ་ ཕྲག་དོག་ གི་ རྒྱུ་ ལས་ གྲུབ་པ་ བཀྲག་མེད་པ་ ཅིག་ ཀྱང་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ འོད་ དང་ ལྷན་ཅིག་ཏུ་ ཁྱོད་ ལ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་བས༔ དེ་ ལ་ ཆགས་སྡང་ མེད་པའི་ བཏང་སྙོམས་ བསྒོམས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: That with together, demigods' light, red, jealousy's cause from formed, lustreless, one, also, wisdom's light with together, you to dawning comes-because: that to, attachment-aversion without's equanimity meditate!
sentences.i: Together with it a dull red light, the light of the demigods, formed from jealousy as its cause, also dawns before you along with the light of wisdom. Toward it, cultivate an equanimity free of attachment and aversion.
sentences.n: As on the fourth day, with the light of the demigods (lha ma yin), which is red, and formed from jealousy (phrag dog), the fifth day's poison; rgyu, 'cause'. lhan cig tu, 'together, along with', where the days before had gshibs mar, 'side by side'. 'ong bas, 'because it comes', runs on to the command. bsgoms shig, 'meditate!, cultivate!': bsgoms is the past stem of sgom, 'to meditate' (sgom / bsgoms / bsgom / sgoms), where the imperative is sgoms, as the print wrote it in 002 (sgoms shig); with shig the form is read as the command: the dull light is to be met with equanimity, where on the fourth day it was not to be delighted in. The other recension has btang snyoms su sgoms shig, 'meditate in equanimity'.

sentences.w: བློ་ དམན་པ་ ཡིན་ ནའང་ དེ་ ལ་ དགའ་བར་ མ་ བྱེད་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Mind weak it-is even-if, that in delight not do!
sentences.i: Even if your understanding is weak, do not take delight in it.
sentences.n: blo, 'mind, understanding'; dman pa, 'low, weak'; yin na'ang, 'even if it is' (na, 'if', with 'ang, 'even', the form of yang after a vowel). Only the print has these words; the other recension has de la dga' ba ma byed cig, 'do not delight in it', alone. Read so, they turn from the one who can rest in equanimity to the one who cannot: he at least must not take pleasure in the dull light.

sentences.w: དེའི་ དུས་སུ་ ཁྱོད་ ཕྲག་དོག་ དྲག་པོས་ དབང་ གིས་ འོད་ ལྗང་ཁུ་ བཀྲག་ ལ་ མཚེར་བ་ དེ་ ལ་ ཁྱོད་ ཞེད་ ནས་ བྲོས་སུ་ འོང་ ཞིང༔
sentences.l: That's time-at, you, jealousy fierce-by(?) power by, light green, lustrous and shimmering, that, at, you, afraid, then, fleeing come, and:
sentences.i: At that time, driven by fierce jealousy, you will be afraid of the green light, lustrous and shimmering, and flee from it,
sentences.n: As on the fourth day, with this day's poison. drag pos dbang gis has drag pos, 'by fierce', where drag po'i, 'of fierce', is meant, as the fourth day has it: 'by the power of fierce jealousy'. zhed, 'to be afraid' (the other recension has bred, of the same sense), where the days before had 'jigs skrag or skrag pa skyes, 'fear arose'. mtsher ba is read as 'tsher ba, 'shimmering', as in the last parts. bros su 'ong zhing, 'come fleeing, and', says what will happen, as before; the other recension has 'ong gi.

sentences.w: ལྷ་མ་ཡིན་ གྱི་ འོད་ དམར་པོ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དེ་ ལ་ ཁྱོད་ དགའ་བ་ དང་ ཆགས་སེམས་ སྐྱེས་ ནས་ འོང་ གིས༔
sentences.l: Demigods' light, red, lustreless, that toward, you, delight and attachment-mind having-arisen, come, and:
sentences.i: and delight and desire for the dull red light of the demigods will arise in you, and you will go toward it.
sentences.n: As on the third day, with skyes, 'arose', where the fourth had bskyed, 'produced'. The other recension has no second khyod, 'you'.

sentences.w: དེ་ཙ་ན་ ཁྱོད་ འོད་ ལྗང་ཁུ་ བཀྲག་ ལ་ མཚེར་བ་ གསལ་ ལ་ དྭངས་པ་ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་པར་ ཡེ་ཤེས་སུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: At-that-time, you, light green, lustrous and shimmering, bright and clear, that at not fearing-way, as-wisdom face-knowing do!
sentences.i: At that time do not be afraid of the green light, lustrous and shimmering, bright and clear: recognise it as wisdom.
sentences.n: As on the days before. mtsher, as above.

sentences.w: དེའི་ ཐོག་ཏུ་ རིག་པ་ བྱར་མེད་ ཀྱི་ ངང་དུ་ གློད་ ལ་ བཞོག་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: That's on-top, knowing nothing-to-do's state-in loosen, and, rest!
sentences.i: Then relax and rest in the state of awareness where there is nothing to do.
sentences.n: As on the fourth day, here with rig pa, 'awareness', in its usual spelling. bzhog cig, 'rest!', is kept as printed: bzhog is none of the regular stems of 'jog, 'to put, to leave' ('jog / bzhag / gzhag / zhog), and it is read as the imperative zhog, which the print has a few lines above and the other recension has here. It may be the print's spelling, as bzhogs shig on the third day, or a cross between bzhag and zhog; which, cannot be told, and the sense is clear. glod, 'loosen, relax' (the other recension klod, the same word).

sentences.w: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ དོན་ཡོད་གྲུབ་པའི་ ཐུགས་རྗེའི་ འོད་ཟེར་ ཡིན་ནོ་ སྐྱབས་སུ་ མཆིའོ༔ སྙམ་པའི་ མོས་གུས་ གྱིས་ ལ་ གསོལ་བ་ ཐོབ་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: 'The Blessed-One Amoghasiddhi's compassion's light-ray it-is; for-refuge I-go' thinking's devotion-respect do, and, prayer obtain(?)!
sentences.i: Think with devotion, 'This is the light of the compassion of the Blessed One Amoghasiddhi; I go to it for refuge', and pray.
sentences.n: The refuge formula of the days before, with Amoghasiddhi's name, and gsol ba thob cig read again, as a guess, as 'pray'. Here it follows the instruction to rest with nothing between: the other recension has yang na, 'or else', before it, and on the fourth day the print began it with de ltar ma shes na, 'if you do not recognise it so'. The print has ༔ after mchi'o, where the days before ran on.

sentences.w: དེ་ ནི་ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ དོན་ཡོད་གྲུབ་པའི་ ཐུགས་རྗེའི་ ལྕགས་ཀྱུའི་ འོད་ཟེར་ བྱ་བ་ གྲུབ་པའི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔ མོས་པ་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: That, as-for: the Blessed-One Amoghasiddhi's compassion's iron-hook's light-ray, deeds accomplished's wisdom so-called it-is. Devotion do!
sentences.i: That is the light of the hook of the compassion of the Blessed One Amoghasiddhi, what is called the wisdom that accomplishes deeds. Turn to it with devotion.
sentences.n: thugs rje'i lcags kyu'i 'od zer, 'the light of the hook of compassion', close to the other recension's wording on the fourth day (thugs rje lcags kyu'i 'od zer), where the print had 'the hook of the light'. zhes bya ba yin no, 'it is what is called', as of the first day's wisdom in 003. The other recension runs on with yin pas, 'because it is', and has de la, 'to it', before mos pa.

sentences.w: མ་ བྲོས་ཤིག༔ བྲོས་ ཀྱང་ ཁྱོད་རང་ དང་ འབྲལ་མེད་དུ་ འོང་ངོ་༔ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Not flee! Fled though, you-yourself with inseparable-as comes. That at not fear!
sentences.i: Do not flee. Even if you flee, it will come with you, never parted from you. Do not be afraid of it.
sentences.n: As on the fourth day, with 'bral med du, 'without parting, inseparably', for 'du 'bral med par, 'without meeting and parting'. bros shig, 'flee!', with ma before it, 'do not flee'.

sentences.w: ལྷ་མ་ཡིན་ གྱི་ འོད་ དམར་པོ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དེ་ ལ་ ཆགས་པར་ མ་ བྱེད་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Demigods' light, red, lustreless, that to attachment not do!
sentences.i: Do not be attached to the dull red light of the demigods.
sentences.n: As on the fourth day.

sentences.w: དེ་ ནི་ ཁྱོད་ ཀྱི་ ཕྲག་དོག་ དྲག་པོས་ བསགས་པའི་ ལས་ ཀྱི་ བསུ་བའི་ ལམ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: That, as-for: your jealousy fierce-by accumulated's karma's welcoming's path it-is.
sentences.i: That is the path on which the karma you have gathered through fierce jealousy comes out to meet you.
sentences.n: The formula of the days before, with las, 'karma, deeds', as the thing gathered, where they had bag chags, 'habitual tendencies' (the first and third days), sdig sgrib, 'sinful obscurations' (the second), or yi dwags, 'the hungry ghosts' (the fourth). The other recension has las kyis bsu ma'i lam, 'the path of the welcomer, by karma'.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ ཆགས་ ན་ ནི་ ཁྱོད་ ལྷ་མ་ཡིན་ གྱི་ གནས་སུ་ ལྷུང་ ནས༔ འཐབ་རྩོད་ ཀྱི་ སྡུག་བསྔལ་ བཟོད་ གླགས་ མེད་པ་ མྱོང་ སྟེ༔
sentences.l: That to attached if, as-for: you, demigods' abode-to fall, then; fighting-quarrel's suffering, bearing chance without, experience, and:
sentences.i: If you are attached to it, you will fall into the abode of the demigods and suffer the fighting and quarrelling there, past bearing.
sentences.n: 'thab rtsod, 'fighting and quarrel', the life of the demigods, who war with the gods out of envy. lhung, the past stem of 'to fall', as on the fourth day (the other recension has ltung, the present and future). bzod glags med pa, 'with no chance to bear it', as there. myong ste runs on.

sentences.w: ཐར་ལམ་ བཀག་པའི་ བར་ཆད་ ཡིན་པས༔ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ ཆགས་པར་ ཞེན་པ་ སྤོངས་ཤིག༔ མ་ ཞེན་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Liberation-path blocked's obstacle it-is-because: that to not attached-way, clinging abandon! Not cling!
sentences.i: It is an obstacle that blocks the path to liberation, so do not be attached to it; give up clinging. Do not cling.
sentences.n: As on the fourth day, with zhen pa spongs shig, 'give up clinging', where the print had chags sems, 'the mind of attachment', there. The other recension has bag chags spongs shig, 'give up the habitual tendencies', in both places. The last two words, ma zhen, stand at the end of p. 56 and cig at the head of p. 57.

sentences.w: འོད་ ལྗང་ཁུ་ གསལ་ ལ་ མཚེར་བ་ དེ་ ལ་ མོས་པ་ གྱིས་ ལ༔ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ དོན་ཡོད་གྲུབ་པ་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ ལ་ འདུན་པ་ རྩེ་གཅིག་ཏུ་ གཏོད་ ལ༔ སྨོན་ལམ་ འདི་སྐད་དུ་ ཐོབ་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Light green, bright and shimmering, that to devotion do, and; the Blessed-One Amoghasiddhi father-mother to aspiration one-pointedly direct, and; prayer these-words-in obtain(?)!
sentences.i: Turn with devotion to the green light, bright and shimmering, direct a single-minded longing to the Blessed One Amoghasiddhi and his consort, and make this prayer:
sentences.n: As on the days before; rtse gcig tu, 'one-pointedly', as on the third day.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་མ་ ཕྲག་དོག་ དྲག་བོས་ འཁོར་བར་ འཁྱམས་པའི་ ཚེ༔ / བྱ་གྲུབ་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ གསལ་བའི་ འོད་ལམ་ ལ༔ / བཅོམ་ལྡན་ དོན་ཡོད་གྲུབ་བས་ ལམ་སྣ་ དྲོངས༔ / ཡུམ་ མཆོག་ དམ་ཚིག་སྒྲོལ་མས་ རྒྱབ་ ནས་ སྐྱོར༔ / བར་དོ་ འཇིགས་པའི་ འཕྲང་ ལས་ བསྒྲལ་དུ་ གསོལ༔ / ཡང་དག་ རྫོགས་པའི་ སངས་རྒྱས་ ས་རུ་ སྐྱོལ༔
sentences.l:
Alas! Jealousy fierce-by in-saṃsāra wandering's time,
the deeds-accomplishing wisdom bright's light-path on,
the Blessed-One Amoghasiddhi-by the-way lead!
The mother supreme Commitment-Saviouress-by from-behind support!
The between fearful's narrow-passage from freeing I-pray;
the genuine perfect buddha's level-to bring!
sentences.i:
Alas! When I wander in saṃsāra through fierce jealousy,
on the bright light-path of the wisdom that accomplishes deeds
may the Blessed One Amoghasiddhi lead the way,
may the supreme mother Samayatārā support me from behind.
I pray you, free me from the fearful narrow passage of the bardo
and bring me to the level of a true and perfect buddha.
sentences.n: The prayer of the days before, with the fifth day's poison, wisdom, buddha and consort, nine syllables to the line. bya grub ye shes is bya ba grub pa'i ye shes, shortened for the metre. drag bos is the print's spelling of drag pos, 'by fierce', its b for p, as in grub bas in the third line (grub pas, 'by Amoghasiddhi'); on the image the first letter of bos may also be p, which would give the regular pos, so the spelling is not sure, though the sense is. sgrol mas, 'by Tārā', with the -s that the second day's consort also had. skyor, 'support!', the present and imperative stem, as on the first day, where the second to fourth days had bskyor, the past and future.

sentences.w: དེ་ལྟར་ མོས་གུས་ དྲག་པོས་ སྨོན་ལམ་ བཏབ་པས༔ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ དོན་ཡོད་གྲུབ་པ་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ གྱི་ ཐུགས་ཀར་ འཇའ་འོད་དུ་ ཐིམ་ ནས༔ བྱང་ཕྱོགས་ ལས་རབ་རྫོགས་པའི་ ཞིང་ཁམས་སུ་ ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་པའི་སྐུར་ སངས་རྒྱས་པར་ འགྱུར་རོ༔
sentences.l: Thus devotion-respect fierce-by, prayer made-because: the Blessed-One Amoghasiddhi father-mother's heart-in as-rainbow-light dissolving, then, the north-direction, Action-Fully-Accomplished's realm-in, as-the-body-of-perfect-enjoyment buddha becomes.
sentences.i: When he makes the prayer in this way with fierce devotion, he dissolves as rainbow light into the heart of the Blessed One Amoghasiddhi and his consort and becomes a buddha in the body of perfect enjoyment in the northern realm of Fully Accomplished Action.
sentences.n: As on the days before, with de ltar, 'thus', where they had de skad, 'those words'. Las rab rdzogs pa, 'Fully Accomplished Action' (las, 'action, deed'; rab, 'very'; rdzogs, 'complete'), is the name the print gives the northern realm here and below, as the other recension does: a name that goes with Amoghasiddhi's wisdom, which accomplishes deeds. las is read as part of the name, not as 'from', because the names of the other realms stand directly after their direction (shar phyogs mngon par dga' ba and the rest, below; nub phyogs bde ba can in 005). The reading is the likelier one, not a sure one: las can also be 'from', and the words would then run 'from the north, into the realm Rab rdzogs pa'. On the fifth day's first appearance (the end of 005) the print has rab brtsegs pa, 'Heaped Up', after las, and there las was taken as 'from'; the other recension has las rab rdzogs pa'i in that place too. Either the print names the realm in two ways, or one of the two places is a slip; the letters are clear in both, and the print is followed in each, so the two parts read las differently.

sentences.w: དེ་ལྟར་ རིམ་བ་ མང་དུ་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པས་ ལས་འཕྲོ་ ཇི་ལྟར་ ཞན་ ཡང་ གཅིག་ ལ་ ངོས་ མ་ ཟིན་ ཀྱང་ གཅིག་ ལ་ ངོས་ ཟིན་ ཏེ་ གང་རུང་ གཅིག་ ལ་ ངོ་ འཕྲོད་ དེ་ མི་ གྲོལ་ མི་ སྲིད་དོ༔
sentences.l: Thus stages many-in face-introduced-because: karmic-residue however weak even, one at recognition not seized though, one at recognition seized, and; whichever one at face meeting, and: not freed not possible.
sentences.i: Pointed out in this way at so many stages, however weak his karmic residue, a person who does not recognise one will recognise another; recognition comes at one or other of them, and it is impossible that he will not be freed.
sentences.n: rim ba is the print's spelling of rim pa, 'stage, step': one light after another, day after day. las 'phro, 'karmic residue' (las, 'karma'; 'phro, 'remainder'), the good karma left over from past lives that ties a person to the teaching. ji ltar zhan yang, 'however weak it is': here the print has zhan, 'weak', where the like sentence of the last part had gzhan, 'other', which gave no clear sense. yang, 'even', is the form the rule gives after -n, where the other recension has kyang, as the print itself writes in ma zin kyang just after. ngos zin, 'to recognise' (ngos, 'side, aspect'; zin, 'seized'), and ngo 'phrod, 'recognition comes' (ngo, 'face'; 'phrod, 'meet'). mi grol mi srid, 'not to be freed is impossible', the double negative of 005.

sentences.w: ཡང་ དེ་ལྟར་ ལན་མང་དུ་ ངོ་སྤྲད་ ཀྱང་ བག་ཆགས་ ཚན་ཆེ་ ལ་ འགྲོགས་ ཡུན་རིང་༔
sentences.l: Again, thus many-times face-introduced though: habitual-tendencies strong, and, associating long,
sentences.i: But though they are pointed out many times in this way, some have strong habitual tendencies and have kept company with them long;
sentences.n: tshan che is read as 'strong, of great force': the habitual tendencies (bag chags) are strong. 'grogs yun ring, 'long associating', as yun ring pa'i in the last part. The print closes the words with ༔ though the sentence goes on; whether a tsheg stands before the ༔ cannot be told on the image, where the stroke of the nga runs on, and the reading does not change. The other recension has yun ring bas, 'because long', running on.

sentences.w: དག་སྣང་ དང་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ སྔར་ འདྲིས་ མེད་པའི་ དབང་ གིས་ ངོ་སྤྲད་ ཀྱང་ བག་ཆགས་ ངན་པས་ ཕྱི་ ལ་ ཁྲིད་ དེ༔
sentences.l: pure-vision and wisdom, before familiarity without's power by, face-introduced though, habitual-tendencies bad-by back-to led, and:
sentences.i: and because they have had no familiarity before with pure vision and wisdom, though they are pointed out, their bad habitual tendencies lead them back.
sentences.n: dag snang, 'pure vision', the world seen as the deities and their realms. sngar 'dris med pa'i dbang gis, 'by the force of not being familiar from before': they did not practise in life. phyi la khrid, 'led back, led away' (phyi, 'behind, outside'; khrid, 'led'): the other recension has phyir la 'khrid, the same.

sentences.w: ཐུགས་རྗེའི་ འོད་ཟེར་ གྱི་ ལྕགས་ཀྱུས་ མ་ ཟིན་པར༔ འོད་ དང་ ཟེར་ ལ་ དངངས་སྐྲག་ སྐྱེས་ ནས་ མར་ ལ་ འཁོར་ ནས༔
sentences.l: Compassion's light-ray's iron-hook-by not seized-way, light and rays at dread-terror having-arisen, then, downward circling, then:
sentences.i: They are not caught by the hook of the light of compassion; dread and terror of the lights and rays arise in them, and they circle on downward.
sentences.n: As in the last part, at the passing of the fourth day, with ma zin par for mi zin par, 'without being caught'. 'khor, 'to circle, to go round', the verb of 'khor ba, saṃsāra, where the fourth day had 'khyams, 'to wander'. mar la, 'downward, onward', as there. The other recension has 'khor bas, 'because they circle', and then de nas, 'then', for da ni, 'now'.

sentences.w: ད་ ནི་ ཞག་ དྲུག་པ་ ལ་ རིགས་ལྔ་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ འཁོར་ དང་ བཅས་པ་ དུས་ གཅིག་ ལ་ འཆར་ ནས་ འོངས་པས༔
sentences.l: Now, day sixth on, the five-families father-mother retinue with together, at-one-time dawning came-because:
sentences.i: Now, on the sixth day, the five families, the buddhas and their consorts with their retinues, come dawning all at once.
sentences.n: zhag drug pa, 'the sixth day'. rigs lnga, 'the five families': the five buddhas of the last days, each with his consort and the deities of his family. 'khor dang bcas pa, 'together with the retinue'. dus gcig la, 'at one time, at once'. 'ongs pas, 'because they have come': 'ongs, the past stem of 'ong, 'to come', with -pas, 'because'; it runs on to the next sentence (the other recension has 'ong ste).

sentences.w: དེའི་ ཚེ་ རིགས་དྲུག་ གི་ འོད་ དྲུག་ ཀྱང་ དུས་ ཅིག་ ལ་ ཤར་ ནས་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: That's time, the six-kinds' lights six also at-one-time dawned, then, come.
sentences.i: At that time the six lights of the six kinds of beings also come, dawning at the same time.
sentences.n: The print has སྐོ at the head of p. 59, a misprint for ངོ, corrected here: p. 58 ends with 'ong, and the syllable that closes the formula 'ong ngo, 'comes', is ngo, as everywhere in the book and in the other recension here; the letters as cut, s over k with the vowel o, give no sense. rigs drug, 'the six kinds', the six realms of rebirth, whose dull lights came one by one beside the wisdom lights. dus cig la, 'at once', is the print's form here of dus gcig la, which it writes just before: cig without its prefix, as in its cig for 'one, a'. shar, 'dawned', the past stem of 'char.

sentences.w: དེ་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ ནི༔ ཚེ་འདས་ ཀྱི་ མིང་ ནས་ བོས་ ལ་ འདི་སྐད་དོ༔ ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔
sentences.l: That face-introduction, as-for: the dead-one's by-name called, and, these-words: O child-of-noble-family!
sentences.i: To point that out, call the dead person by name and say this: O child of noble family,
sentences.n: The formula of the days before, with de, 'that', at its head. bos is the past and imperative stem of 'bod, 'to call' ('bod / bos / bod / bos), where the days before had 'bod or bod; the other recension has 'bod. The print has no 'listen without distraction' here, as the days before had and the other recension has; it comes a few lines below.

sentences.w: ཁྱོད་ ཁ་སང་ ཕན་ཆད་ རིགས་ལྔ་ སོ་སོའི་ སྣང་བ་ ཤར་ ནས༔ ངོ་སྤྲད་ ཀྱང་ ཁྱོད་ བག་ཆགས་ ཀྱི་ དབང་ གིས་ དེ་ ལ་ སྐྲག་དངངས་ སྐྱེས་པས་ ད་ ཕན་ཆད་དུ་ འདིར་ ལུས་པ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: You, yesterday up-to, five-families each's appearance dawned, then, face-introduced though, you, habitual-tendencies' power by, that at fright-terror having-arisen-because: now up-to here remained it-is.
sentences.i: Until yesterday the visions of each of the five families dawned for you, and they were pointed out to you, but through the force of your habitual tendencies terror arose in you at them, and so you have stayed here until now.
sentences.n: kha sang phan chad, 'until yesterday', as in 003; da phan chad du, 'until now'. so so'i, 'of each one'. skrag dngangs, 'fright and terror', the two words of dngangs skrag in the other order. lus pa yin no, 'it is that you have remained, been left behind'. The other recension has bag chags ngan pa'i dbang gis, 'through the force of bad habitual tendencies'.

sentences.w: ཁྱོད་ ཀྱི་ གོང་དུ་ རིགས་ལྔའི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ རང་མདངས་ དེ་ རྣམས་ རང་སྣང་དུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་ ན་ རིགས་ལྔ་ སོ་སོའི་ སྐུ་ ལ་ འཇའ་འོད་དུ་ ཐིམ་ ནས་ ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་པའི་སྐུ་རུ་ སངས་རྒྱས་ རྒྱུ་ ཡིན་པ་ ལ༔
sentences.l: You-of(by?) earlier-at, five-families' wisdom's own-radiances those (plural) as-self-appearance face know if, five-families each's bodies in as-rainbow-light dissolving, then, as-the-body-of-perfect-enjoyment buddha-becoming was-to-be, whereas:
sentences.i: Before this, if you had recognised those natural radiances of the wisdoms of the five families as your own appearance, you would have dissolved as rainbow light into the bodies of each of the five families and become a buddha in the body of perfect enjoyment;
sentences.n: gong du, 'earlier, before this' (gong, 'above, before', with du). khyod kyi has kyi, 'of', where the sense wants kyis, 'by', marking 'you' as the one who recognises, as the other recension has it (khyod kyis); it is read so, as the print writes gi for gis elsewhere (gcig gi in the pilot). rang snang du ngo shes na, 'if you recognise them as your own appearance', the words of 003 for the visions of the bardo. sangs rgyas rgyu yin pa, 'it was to be that you became a buddha': rgyu after a verb marks what is to happen. la after yin pa, 'whereas, but', turns to what did happen.

sentences.w: རང་སྣང་དུ་ མ་ ཤེས་པས༔ འདིར་ འཁྱམས་པ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: As-self-appearance not knowing-because, here wandering it-is.
sentences.i: but because you did not know them as your own appearance, you are wandering here.
sentences.n: The other recension has 'because you did not recognise them, until now (ngo ma shes pas da bar du) you have wandered here'; the print names what was not recognised, the visions as one's own appearance.

sentences.w: ད་ ནི་ མ་ ཡེངས་པར་ ཉོན་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Now not distracted-way listen!
sentences.i: Now listen without distraction.
sentences.n: The words that follow the call in the formula of the days before stand here. The other recension has ltos shig, 'look!'.

sentences.w: རིགས་ལྔ་ ཡོངས་རྫོགས་ ཀྱི་ སྣང་བ་ དང༔ ཡེ་ཤེས་ བཞི་ སྦྱོར་ གྱི་ སྣང་བ་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ་ ཁྱོད་ བསུ་བ་ ལ་ འོང་ངོ་༔ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Five-families complete's appearance and; wisdoms four joined's appearance so-called, you meeting for comes. Face-knowing do!
sentences.i: What is called the vision of the five families complete and the vision of the four wisdoms joined is coming to meet you. Recognise it.
sentences.n: The print has ཁྱ་བ, a misprint for བྱ་བ, corrected here: the letter is plainly kha, but only bya ba, 'what is called', gives sense after zhes, and the other recension has it. yongs rdzogs, 'complete, all together': the five families now come at once. ye shes bzhi sbyor, 'the four wisdoms joined' (sbyor, 'to join, to unite'): four, not five, as the four lights of the next sentence. The other recension has khyod la bsu ba la, 'to meet you', with la after khyod.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ འབྱུང་བ་ བཞིའི་ རྣམ་པར་ དག་པའི་ འོད་ ཁ་དོག་ བཞི་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! The four elements' completely pure's lights, colours four, dawning come.
sentences.i: O child of noble family, the lights of the four elements, wholly purified, will dawn in four colours.
sentences.n: The four elements of the second to fifth days, water, earth, fire and wind, with their white, yellow, red and green lights. 'byung ba bzhi'i, 'of the four elements', has the 'of' ending on bzhi, 'four'; the other recension has bzhi without it.

sentences.w: དེའི་ དུས་སུ་ དབུས་ཕྱོགས་ ཐིག་ལེ་བརྡལ་བའི་ ཞིང་ཁམས་ ནས༔ སངས་རྒྱས་ རྣམ་པར་སྣང་མཛད་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ གོང་ ལྟར་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: That's time-at, the centre-direction, Spread-Drop's realm from, the Buddha Vairocana father-mother, above like, dawning come.
sentences.i: At that time, from the central realm called the Spreading Drop, the Buddha Vairocana and his consort will dawn as before.
sentences.n: The five buddhas come now in the order of the five days, each from his realm. gong ltar, 'as above, as before': as he dawned on the first day. Here sangs rgyas, 'buddha', stands before each name, where the days before had bcom ldan 'das, 'Blessed One' (on the fifth day both).

sentences.w: ཤར་ཕྱོགས་ མངོན་པར་དགའ་བའི་ ཞིང་ཁམས་ ནས༔ སངས་རྒྱས་ རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའ་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ འཁོར་ དང་ བཅས་པ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: The east-direction, Manifest-Joy's realm from, the Buddha Vajrasattva father-mother retinue with together, dawning come.
sentences.i: From the eastern realm of Manifest Joy the Buddha Vajrasattva and his consort will dawn with their retinue.
sentences.n: As on the second day; 'khor dang bcas pa, 'with the retinue', the bodhisattvas around each pair.

sentences.w: ལྷོ་ཕྱོགས་ དཔལ་ དང་ ལྡན་པའི་ ཞིང་ཁམས་ ནས༔ སངས་རྒྱས་ རིན་ཆེན་འབྱུང་ལྡན་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ འཁོར་ དང་ བཅས་པ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: The south-direction, Glory-with-Endowed's realm from, the Buddha Ratnasambhava father-mother retinue with together, dawning come.
sentences.i: From the southern realm Endowed with Glory the Buddha Ratnasambhava and his consort will dawn with their retinue.
sentences.n: As on the third day.

sentences.w: ནུབ་ཕྱོགས་ པདྨ་བརྩེགས་པ་ བདེ་བ་ཅན་ གྱི་ ཞིང་ཁམས་ ནས༔ སངས་རྒྱས་ སྣང་བ་མཐའ་ཡས་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ འཁོར་ དང་ བཅས་པ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: The west-direction, Lotus-Heaped, the-Blissful's realm from, the Buddha Amitābha father-mother retinue with together, dawning come.
sentences.i: From the western realm of Bliss, the Heaped Lotuses, the Buddha Amitābha and his consort will dawn with their retinue.
sentences.n: As on the fourth day. padma brtsegs pa, 'lotuses heaped up' (brtsegs, 'stacked'), stands before Bde ba can, 'the Blissful', as a second name of the western realm, or a description of it; the text does not say which.

sentences.w: བྱང་ཕྱོགས་ ལས་རབ་རྫོགས་པའི་ ཞིང་ཁམས་ ནས༔ སངས་རྒྱས་ དོན་ཡོད་གྲུབ་པ་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ འཁོར་ དང་ བཅས་པ་ འཇའ་ དང་ འོད་ ཀྱི་ ཀློང་ ནས་ ཁྱོད་ ལ་ ད་ལྟ་ འཆར་རོ༔
sentences.l: The north-direction, Action-Fully-Accomplished's realm from, the Buddha Amoghasiddhi father-mother retinue with together, rainbow and light's expanse from, you to now dawn.
sentences.i: And from the northern realm of Fully Accomplished Action the Buddha Amoghasiddhi and his consort, with their retinue, now dawn before you out of an expanse of rainbow and light.
sentences.n: As on the fifth day, with Las rab rdzogs pa for the realm, as above. da lta 'char ro, 'now dawn', the present, where the others had 'char du 'ong ngo, 'will come to dawn'. The other recension has 'ja' 'od kyi klong, 'an expanse of rainbow light'.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ རིགས་ལྔ་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ དེ་ རྣམས་ ཀྱི་ ཕྱི་རིམ་དུ༔ སྒོ་བ་ ཁྲོ་བོ་ རྣམ་པར་རྒྱལ་བ་ དང་༔ གཤིན་རྗེ་གཤེད་པོ་ དང་༔ རྟ་མགྲིན་རྒྱལ་པོ་ དང་༔ བདུད་རྩི་འཁྱིལ་པ་ དང་༔ སྒོ་མ་ ལྕགས་ཀྱུ་མ་ དང་༔ ཞགས་པ་མ་ དང་༔ ལྕགས་སྒྲོག་མ་ དང་༔ དྲིལ་བུ་མ་ དང་༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! The five-families father-mother those (plural)'s outer-tier-in: the gatekeepers, wrathful-ones Fully-Victorious and Death-Lord-Slayer and Horse-Neck-King and Nectar-Coil and; the gate-women Iron-Hook-Lady and Noose-Lady and Iron-Chain-Lady and Bell-Lady and;
sentences.i: O child of noble family, in the outer ring around those five families, the buddhas and their consorts, the gatekeepers will dawn too, the wrathful ones Vijaya, Yamāntaka, King Hayagrīva and Amṛtakuṇḍalin, and the gatekeeper goddesses Aṅkuśā, Pāśā, Śṛṅkhalā and Ghaṇṭā;
sentences.n: The print has གཞིན་རྗེ, a misprint for གཤིན་རྗེ, corrected here: the image shows zh, but only gshin gives the name, and the other recension has gshin rje'i gshed po. The sentence runs on through the next unit to its verb, 'char ro, 'dawn'. phyi rim, 'the outer tier, the outer ring' (the other recension phyi rol, 'outside'): the gates of the circle of deities face the four directions. sgo ba, 'gatekeeper', and sgo ma, the female gatekeeper; khro bo, 'wrathful one'. The four male names: Rnam par rgyal ba, 'Fully Victorious' (Vijaya); Gshin rje gshed po, 'Slayer of the Lord of Death' (Yamāntaka; gshin rje, 'lord of the dead'); Rta mgrin rgyal po, 'Horse-Neck, the king' (Hayagrīva); Bdud rtsi 'khyil pa, 'Coil of Nectar' (Amṛtakuṇḍalin). The goddesses are named for what they hold, each with the female ending -ma: lcags kyu, 'iron hook'; zhags pa, 'noose'; lcags sgrog, 'iron chain'; dril bu, 'bell'.

sentences.w: ལྷའི་ ཐུབ་པ་ དབང་པོ་བརྒྱ་བྱིན་ དང་༔ ལྷ་མ་ཡིན་ གྱི་ ཐུབ་པ་ ཐག་བཟང་རིས་ དང་༔ མིའི་ ཐུབ་པ་ ཤཱཀྱ་སེངྒེ་ དང་༔ བྱོལ་སོང་ ཐུབ་པ་ སེངྒེ་རབ་བརྟན་ དང་༔ ཡི་དྭགས་ ཀྱི་ ཐུབ་པ་ ཁ་འབར་མ་ དང་༔ དམྱལ་བའི་ ཐུབ་པ་ ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་པོ་ དང་༔ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ ཐུབ་པ་ དྲུག་ ཀྱང་ འཆར་རོ༔
sentences.l: the gods' sage Lord-Hundred-Offerings and; the demigods' sage Good-Weave-Pattern and; humans' sage Śākya-Lion and; animal sage Lion-Very-Firm and; hungry-ghosts' sage Blazing-Mouth and; hell's sage Dharma's-King and: the Blessed-One sages six also dawn.
sentences.i: and the six sages, the Blessed Ones, will dawn too: the sage of the gods, Indra Śatakratu; the sage of the demigods, Vemacitra; the sage of humans, Śākyasiṃha; the sage of animals, Steadfast Lion; the sage of the hungry ghosts, Blazing Mouth; and the sage of the hells, the King of the Teaching.
sentences.n: thub pa, 'sage, the able one' (Sanskrit muni): in each of the six realms of rebirth a buddha appears as a sage to teach its beings. Dbang po brgya byin, 'Lord of a Hundred Offerings', is Indra, called Śatakratu, 'of a hundred sacrifices'. Thag bzang ris, word by word 'good-weave-pattern', is the king of the demigods, Vemacitra. Shākya seng ge, 'Lion of the Śākyas', is the Buddha of our age; the other recension has Shākya thub pa, 'Sage of the Śākyas', Śākyamuni. byol song, 'animal', here without kyi, 'of' (the other recension byol song gi); Seng ge rab brtan, 'the very steadfast lion'. Kha 'bar ma, 'Blazing Mouth' (kha, 'mouth'; 'bar, 'to blaze'), with -ma, which usually marks a woman. Chos kyi rgyal po, 'King of the Teaching' (Sanskrit dharmarāja). For the sages of the animals and the hungry ghosts the Tibetan names are given word by word.

sentences.w: ཀུན་ཏུ་བཟང་པོ་ དང༔ ཀུན་ཏུ་བཟང་མོ་ དང༔ སངས་རྒྱས་ ཐམས་ཅད་ ཀྱི་ སྤྱི་མེས་ ཀུན་བཟང་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ གཉིས་ ཀྱང་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: the All-Good and; the All-Good-Lady and; buddhas all's forefather, All-Good father-mother, two, also dawning come.
sentences.i: Samantabhadra and Samantabhadrī, the forefather of all the buddhas, the All-Good father and mother, the two of them, will dawn too.
sentences.n: Kun tu bzang po, 'the All-Good' (Samantabhadra), is here the primordial buddha of 002, not the bodhisattva of the third day, and Kun tu bzang mo his consort, named in 002 as reality itself; kun bzang is the short form of the name. spyi mes, 'common ancestor, forefather' (spyi, 'general, of all'; mes, 'grandfather'; the other recension spyi myes).

sentences.w: ལོངས་སྐུའི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ བཞི་བཅུ་རྩ་གཉིས་ སྙིང་ གི་ ནང་ ནས་ ཐོན་ ནས་ ཁྱོད་རང་ ལ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་བས༔ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ དག་པའི་ སྣང་བ་ ལས་ འཆར་བ་ ཡིན་པས་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: The enjoyment-body's deity-host forty-two, heart's inside from emerging, then, you-yourself to dawning come-because: you-yourself's pure appearance from dawning it-is-because, face-knowing do!
sentences.i: The forty-two deities of the body of enjoyment come out from within your heart and dawn before you. They arise from your own pure vision: recognise them.
sentences.n: longs sku, 'enjoyment body', short for longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku. The forty-two are those just named: five buddhas and five consorts, eight bodhisattvas and eight female bodhisattvas, eight gatekeepers, six sages, and the All-Good pair. bzhi bcu rtsa gnyis, 'forty-two' (bzhi bcu, 'forty'; rtsa joins the units to the tens). thon, 'to come out, to emerge'. 'char du 'ong bas and 'char ba yin pas both end in -s, 'because', and both run on to the command. dag pa'i snang ba las 'char ba, 'arising from your pure vision'; the other recension has la, 'in, to', 'arising in your pure vision'.

sentences.w: ཀྱེ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ ཞིང་ཁམས་ དེ་ དག་ ཀྱང་ གཞན་ ཞིག་ ན་ ཡོད་པ་ ནི་ མ་ ཡིན་ ཏེ༔ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ སྙིང་ གི་ ཕྱོགས་ བཞི་ དབུས་ དང་ ལྔ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! Realms those (plural) also, another somewhere in existing, as-for, are-not, and: you-yourself's heart's quarters four, centre with, five they-are.
sentences.i: O child of noble family, these realms too are not somewhere else: they are the four quarters and the centre of your own heart, five in all.
sentences.n: kye, 'O', is the print's other spelling of kyai, which it uses beside it. gzhan zhig na, 'in some other place'; yod pa ni ma yin, 'it is not that they are'. phyogs bzhi dbus dang lnga, 'the four quarters with the centre, five'. The other recension says the realms abide in (na gnas pa) the four quarters and centre of the heart; the print says they are them.

sentences.w: སྙིང་ གི་ ནང་ ནས་ ད་ལྟ་ ཕྱིར་ ཐོན་ ནས་ ཁྱོད་རང་ ལ་ འཆར་བ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: Heart's inside from now outward emerging, then, you-yourself to dawning it-is.
sentences.i: They are coming out from within your heart now and dawning before you.
sentences.n: phyir thon, 'to come out, outward' (phyir, 'outward').

sentences.w: སྐུ་ དེ་ དག་ ཀྱང་ གཞན་ ཞིག་ ནས་ འོང་བ་ མ་ ཡིན་ ཏེ༔ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ རིག་པའི་ རང་རྩལ་ ལས་ ཡེ་ནས་ ལྷུན་གྱིས་གྲུབ་པ་ ཡིན་པས༔ དེ་ལྟར་ ཡིན་པར་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Bodies those (plural) also, another somewhere from coming are-not, and: you-yourself's knowing's own-energy from, from-the-beginning spontaneously-present it-is-because, thus it-is, face-knowing do!
sentences.i: These forms too do not come from somewhere else. They are present of themselves from the very beginning, out of the natural energy of your own awareness: recognise that it is so.
sentences.n: ye nas, 'from the very first, primordially', here without a negative. lhun gyis grub pa, 'present of itself, spontaneously accomplished' (lhun, 'a mass, of itself'; grub pa, 'accomplished'), a fixed term for what is there without being made. The other recension has ye nas grub pa only, without lhun gyis; in the print the letters of gyis are not sure on the image, where they may also be kyi, and gyis, the usual form of the term, is read. rang rtsal las, 'out of the natural energy'; the other recension has la. The part ends here; the next sentence of the print speaks of the size of the forms.
